1.title: Timed Mixed Lab Set B
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Timed Mixed Lab Set B. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. How to use this set. Review after the set. Practice with sixteen timed tasks worth one hundred six points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Troubleshooting five tasks, Cluster Architecture four, Services and Networking three, Workloads two, Storage two). Practice in this module: sixteen tasks, one hundred six points, about one hundred ten minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: How to use this set
1.text: How to use this set. Same rules as Set A (Module fourteen): a one hundred twenty-minute timer, only the allowed documentation, each task prepared with the setup flag, all-or-nothing scoring with the check flag, pass mark sixty-six percent of the points. This set uses different tasks from Set A, so do Set A first, then B a few days later. Honest note: the tasks come from the module labs; they test speed and routine, not surprise. For surprise use the killer dot S H simulator. Exam tip: Do Set A first and Set B a few days later, so you can see whether your routine improved.

1.title: Review after the set
1.text: Review after the set. Compare your score with Set A. Which domain improved, which did not? List every command you had to look up. Learn the five most frequent ones by heart. Redo the three slowest tasks cold. Exam tip: Compare your domain scores with Set A and redo the three slowest tasks.

1.title: Task 1: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task one: Troubleshooting. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The node C K A worker went Not Ready after someone edited the kubelet configuration. Find the problem in the kubelet logs, fix the configuration file slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml on that node, and bring the node back to Ready. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 1: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker system control status kubelet the no pager flag head -eight. Then S S H C K A worker journal control dash u kubelet the no pager flag grep dash i dash E yaml failed error tail -three. Then S S H C K A worker sed dash i or ^broken slash d slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml system control restart kubelet. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Ready node slash C K A worker the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 2: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task two: Troubleshooting. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app four, the Pods of the Deployment worker crash with a clear message in their logs. Read the log, then fix the Deployment (do not change the image or the command) so that the Pods run stably with the required setting D B H O S T db dot internal. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 2: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app four logs deploy slash worker the tail flag set to three. Then kube control dash n app four set env deployment worker D B H O S T db dot internal. Then kube control dash n app four rollout status deployment worker the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 3: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task three: Troubleshooting. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace net four, the Service web has endpoints, but requests to H T T P colon slash slash web dot net four end with "connection refused". The Pods are Ready and the engine X containers listen on port eighty. Fix the Service (do not touch the Deployment) so that H T T P colon slash slash web dot net four works. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 3: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n net four get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name web dash o wide. Then kube control dash n net four describe svc web then pipe to grep dash i dash E Port then pipe to Endpoints. Then kube control dash n net four patch svc web the type flag set to json dash p op replace, path slash spec slash ports slash zero slash target Port, value eighty. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 4: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task four: Troubleshooting. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace app seven, the Pod api is stuck in Init zero slash one: its init container waits until the D N S name db resolves inside the namespace. Without changing the Pod, make the Pod start. The name db must be the name of a Service in app seven that selects the existing Pod database (label app database, engine X on port eighty). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 4: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n app seven get pod api. Then kube control dash n app seven logs api dash c wait db the tail flag set to three. Then kube control dash n app seven expose pod database the name flag set to db the port flag set to eighty. Then kube control dash n app seven wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash api the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 5: Troubleshooting
1.text: Task five: Troubleshooting. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace cm one, the Deployment counter (two replicas) was created but no Pods appear and kube control get rs shows nothing. Find the faulty control plane component on C K A control plane and repair it so that both Pods run. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 5: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube controller manager. Then S S H C K A control plane C R I C T L logs C R I C T L ps dash a the name flag kube controller manager dash q head -one, and so on. Then S S H C K A control plane sed dash i s ca dot crtx ca dot crt slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash kube controller manager dot yaml. Then S S H C K A control plane system control restart kubelet resets the crash loop back off of the static Pod. Then kube control dash n cm one rollout status deployment counter the timeout flag set to one hundred eighty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 6: Architecture
1.text: Task six: Architecture. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create the namespace ci and a Service Account deployer in it. Create a Cluster Role deploy manager that allows get, list, create and update on deployments in the apps A P I group. Grant it to the Service Account only inside the namespace ci (not cluster-wide). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 6: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control create ns ci. Then kube control dash n ci create serviceaccount deployer. Then kube control create clusterrole deploy manager the verb flag set to get,list,create,update the resource flag set to deployments dot apps. Then kube control dash n ci create rolebinding deploy manager the clusterrole flag set to deploy manager the serviceaccount flag set to ci deployer. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 7: Architecture
1.text: Task seven: Architecture. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Node C K A worker two needs maintenance. Make it unschedulable and evict the workloads from it, leaving the Daemon Set Pods alone (Pods that use empty dir volumes may be deleted). A Deployment web in the namespace maint (four replicas) must still have all four replicas Ready afterwards, on the other nodes. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 7: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control drain C K A worker two the ignore daemonsets flag the delete emptydir data flag. Then kube control dash n maint rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Task 8: Architecture
1.text: Task eight: Architecture. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. A Kustomize base exists in about slash kust slash base (a Deployment web with one replica and a Service web ). Create an overlay in about slash kust slash overlays slash prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, three replicas, and the container image to engine X stable alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Task 8: Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. cat about slash kust slash overlays slash prod slash customization dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash prod then pipe to head -thirty. Then kube control create ns prod. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash prod. Then kube control dash n prod rollout status deployment prod web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 9: Architecture
2.text: Task nine: Architecture. This task is worth five points, and you should plan about five minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create a static Pod named static web with image engine X alpine on the node C K A worker. Find the directory the kubelet watches for static Pod manifests from the kubelet configuration file. The Pod must run in the default namespace. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 9: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run S S H C K A worker grep static Pod Path slash var slash lib slash kubelet slash config dot yaml. S S H C K A worker mkdir dash p slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests cat slash E T C slash Kubernetes slash manifests slash static web dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 10: Troubleshooting
2.text: Task ten: Troubleshooting. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace svc three, the Service api does not work: requests to H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three hang. The Deployment api (two replicas) is healthy. Find the cause and fix the Service without changing the Deployment, so that H T T P colon slash slash api dot svc three returns the engine X welcome page. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 10: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n svc three get endpointslices dash l Kubernetes dot io slash service name api. Then kube control dash n svc three get svc api dash o json path dot spec dot selector echo. Then kube control dash n svc three get pods the show labels flag. Then kube control dash n svc three patch svc api dash p spec selector app api. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 11: Networking
2.text: Task eleven: Networking. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace np three, the Pod app (busy box) must only be allowed to send traffic to (a) Pods labelled app db on T C P port eighty and (b) the cluster D N S on port fifty-three (U D P and T C P). All other outgoing traffic from app must be blocked. Create one Network Policy named app egress for the Pod app. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 11: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control dash n np three apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then sleep five. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 12: Troubleshooting
2.text: Task twelve: Troubleshooting. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace net five, the Pod lookup cannot resolve any cluster names (for example Kubernetes dot default ). Find the cause in the Pod spec and recreate the Pod lookup (image busy box one dot thirty-six, command sleep three thousand six hundred ) so that it uses the cluster D N S and can resolve Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 12: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n net five get pod lookup dash o json path dot spec dot dns Policy newline. Then kube control dash n net five exec lookup -- cat slash E T C slash resolv dot conf. Then kube control dash n net five delete pod lookup the force flag the grace period flag zero. Then kube control dash n net five run lookup the image flag set to busy box one dot thirty-six the command flag -- sleep three thousand six hundred. Then kube control dash n net five wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash lookup the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n net five exec lookup -- N S lookup Kubernetes dot default dot svc dot cluster dot local. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 13: Workloads
2.text: Task thirteen: Workloads. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace probes, the Deployment site (two replicas, engine X alpine ) has no health checks. Add to its container. a readiness probe: H T T P get or on port eighty, initial Delay Seconds three, period Seconds five. a liveness probe: H T T P get or on port eighty, initial Delay Seconds ten, period Seconds ten. All replicas must be Ready afterwards. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 13: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n probes patch deployment site dash p spec template spec containers name engine X, readiness Probe http Get path or, port eighty, initial Delay Seconds three, period Seconds five, liveness Probe, and so on. Then kube control dash n probes rollout status deployment site the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 14: Workloads
2.text: Task fourteen: Workloads. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Taint the node C K A worker two with dedicated db No Schedule. In the namespace taint, create a Pod db (image engine X alpine ) that tolerates this taint and is placed on C K A worker two using node selector on the label Kubernetes dot io slash hostname. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 14: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control taint node C K A worker two dedicated db No Schedule. kube control dash n taint apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control dash n taint wait the for flag set to condition Ready pod slash db the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 15: Troubleshooting
2.text: Task fifteen: Troubleshooting. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. In the namespace st six, the Pod app is stuck Pending because its Persistent Volume Claim app data does not bind. Find the cause and fix it so the Pod runs with the claim bound. Keep the names app and app data, the size one gibibyte and Read Write Once. (A claim's Storage Class cannot be edited in place; recreate what is needed.). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 15: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control dash n st six describe pod app then pipe to grep dash i -A two Failed Scheduling. Then kube control dash n st six describe pvc app data then pipe to grep dash i -A two events. Then kube control get sc. Then kube control dash n st six delete pod app the force flag the grace period flag zero. Then kube control dash n st six delete pvc app data. kube control dash n st six apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 15: Solution, continued
2.text: Task fifteen: Solution, continued. Run ---. Then api Version version one. Then kind Pod. Then metadata name app. Then spec. Then containers. Then - name main. Then image busy box one dot thirty-six. Then command sleep, three thousand six hundred. The remaining lines are on the screen.

2.title: Task 16: Storage
2.text: Task sixteen: Storage. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Create a Persistent Volume pv manual with capacity two gibibytes, access mode Read Write Once, reclaim policy Retain, Storage Class name manual and the host path slash mnt slash data. In the namespace st two, create a Persistent Volume Claim claim requesting one gibibyte, Read Write Once, Storage Class manual. The claim must be bound to pv manual. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Task 16: Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. kube control apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Task 16: Solution, continued
2.text: Task sixteen: Solution, continued. kube control dash n st two apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then sleep three. Then kube control dash n st two get pvc claim.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Why do Sets A and B use different tasks? Answer: So the second set tests the routine again without repeating the same answers. Question two. What does a score of sixty percent mean for your readiness? Answer: Below the sixty-six percent pass mark: repeat the weakest domain's labs and redo the set. Question three. What should you do first when the cluster context may be wrong? Answer: Run the context line and check kube control config current context.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which flag generates a manifest without creating the object? Answer: the dry run flag set to client dash o yaml. Question five. What do you check after fixing a broken node or component? Answer: The original symptom: kube control get nodes or a test Pod. Question six. How many minutes should you keep for review at the end? Answer: About ten.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Set B: sixteen tasks, one hundred twenty minutes, sixty-six percent to pass, docs allowed. Different from A: do A first, B a few days later. After: compare domain scores, redo the slowest three. In the next module, we continue the course.
